assignments.html:
This item appears in the grade book and only is for scholars who are currently failing the course. It is not an assignment and it is worth 0 points.

No action is required from the scholar.

 

The purpose of this placeholder is simply to mark scholars who have not passed the course this quarter.

It allows the teacher to quickly identify which scholars may need guidance, check-ins, or future opportunities to demonstrate understanding of the material.

This is simply a signal to pause, review your progress, and connect with your teacher if support is needed.

 

Again, there is nothing to submit and nothing to complete for this item. It is only a marker for academic support.

quizzes.title: 🏛 Earth’s Interior, Plate Tectonics & Surface Changes Quiz

questions.text: What is the main source of energy that drives movement inside Earth?
Convection causes hot material to sink and cool material to rise.
Which Earth layer allows material to flow slowly and helps tectonic plates move?
Earthquakes usually happen suddenly and are considered rapid changes to Earth’s surface.
Which type of plate boundary forms when plates move AWAY from each other and new crust is created?
Mountain building happens quickly and usually occurs during earthquakes.
What happens at a transform plate boundary?

answers.text: Magma rises and creates new crust
Plates slide past each other and stress builds

questions.text: Volcanoes are evidence that Earth’s interior is active and contains heat.
Which surface feature forms when plates move apart and magma cools to create new oceanic crust?
Tectonic plates move several kilometers per year across Earth’s surface.
Sedimentary rocks often form in layers.
Which rock type forms when melted rock cools and hardens?
Weathering and erosion are the same process.
Which process moves sediment from one place to another?
Which rock type forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure without melting?
The rock cycle has a clear beginning and a clear ending.
Which process happens when sediment is dropped and builds up in layers?
Plate tectonics can create igneous rocks and change rocks into metamorphic rocks
What is sediment?

answers.text: Small pieces of rock or material

questions.text: Which set of processes can directly change rock deep underground?

quizzes.title: 🏛 Earth’s Age & Evidence of Change Over Time Quiz

questions.text: Which method gives the exact age in years of a rock or fossil?
Fossils provide evidence that life on Earth has changed over time.
According to the law of superposition, which rock layer is usually the oldest?
Scientific theories are guesses that are not based on evidence.
What does half-life describe?

answers.text: Time for half of a radioactive element to decay
Time for a rock to form

questions.text: Geologic time refers to the very long history of Earth.
Which provides evidence that continents were once connected?

answers.text: Similar fossils and rocks on different continents

questions.text: Relative age dating tells the exact number of years an object has existed.
Which is an example of physical evidence showing Earth’s past?
Scientists often use both relative dating and radioactive dating together to understand Earth’s history.
Which Earth layer allows heated material to move slowly through convection?
What type of rock forms from compacted and cemented sediment?
Which plate boundary occurs when plates slide past each other?
What is half-life?

answers.text: Time for half of a radioactive element to decay
Time for a rock to melt
Time for a mountain to form

questions.text: Which provides evidence that continents were once connected?

answers.text: Matching fossils and rocks on different continents

questions.text: What type of rock forms when magma or lava cools?
Which human activity can increase erosion by removing plant roots?
What causes tectonic plates to move?
Which method gives the exact age of rocks?
Which surface change usually happens quickly?
What is magma?
Which rock type forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure?
What does the law of superposition state?

answers.text: Older rocks are always on top
Older layers are usually below younger layers
Rocks form at the same time

questions.text: Which process can make land dry and less productive over time?
What evidence do fossils provide?

answers.text: Life existed long ago and has changed over time

questions.text: What forms when continental plates collide?
Which event releases energy as seismic waves?
Which process breaks rock into smaller pieces at Earth’s surface?
Which human activity can reduce water quality?
What is a scientific theory?

answers.text: A well-tested explanation supported by evidence

questions.text: Which boundary builds new crust when plates move apart?
Why do mountains take millions of years to form?
Which process can create igneous rocks underground?
What kind of evidence includes fault lines and lava flows?
How do dams affect Earth’s systems?

answers.text: Change water flow and sediment movement

quizzes.title: 🏛 Thermal Energy and Phase Changes Quiz

questions.text: What is heat?

answers.text: A measure of how fast particles move
Energy that moves from a warmer object to a cooler object
A type of particle in matter

questions.text: What does temperature measure?

answers.text: The amount of heat in the atmosphere
The size of particles in matter
The amount of matter in an object
The speed at which particles are moving

questions.text: What happens to particles when heat is added to a substance?
Which change of state occurs when heat is removed from a liquid?
What may happen during a change of state?

answers.text: Temperature may stay the same while particles rearrange

quizzes.title: 🏛 Temperature Differences and Energy Balance Quiz

questions.text: In which direction does heat naturally flow?

answers.text: From cooler objects to warmer objects
From warmer objects to cooler objects
From larger objects to smaller objects

questions.text: Why does heat flow between objects?

answers.text: Because particles move at different speeds in objects with different temperatures
Because gravity pulls heat toward Earth

questions.text: What happens when two objects reach thermal equilibrium?

answers.text: Both objects reach the same temperature and heat flow stops
The warmer object becomes colder than the cooler object

questions.text: What is a system in the study of heat transfer?

answers.text: The heat source in a room
The object or group of objects being studied

questions.text: What happens over time when a hot object and a cold object interact?

answers.text: Both objects immediately stop changing temperature
Heat flows until both objects reach the same temperature

quizzes.title: 🏛 Understanding the Law of Conservation of Energy Quiz

questions.text: What does the Law of Conservation of Energy state?

answers.text: Energy only exists in the form of heat
Energy can be destroyed but not created
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or transformed
Energy can be created but not destroyed

questions.text: What is energy?

answers.text: The force that pulls objects toward Earth
The ability to cause change or do work
The movement of particles in the atmosphere

questions.text: Which example shows an energy transfer?

answers.text: Heat moving from hot soup into a metal spoon
Electrical energy turning into light in a bulb
Chemical energy turning into motion when riding a bike

questions.text: Which example shows an energy transformation?

answers.text: Water flowing downhill in a river
Heat moving from a warm object to a cooler one
Electrical energy changing into light and heat in a light bulb

questions.text: When a moving object slows down due to friction, what happens to the energy?

quizzes.title: 🏛 Energy Transformations and Evidence of Conservation Quiz

questions.text: What happens during an energy transformation?

answers.text: Energy changes from one form to another
Energy stops moving in a system

questions.text: Which example shows an energy transformation?

answers.text: Electrical energy changing into light and heat in a toaster
Heat moving from hot soup to a spoon
A ball sitting still on the ground

questions.text: What is a system in the study of energy?

answers.text: A group of planets in space
The object or group of objects being studied

questions.text: What evidence might show that energy has transformed rather than disappeared?

answers.text: Temperature increases or heat is produced

questions.text: According to the Law of Conservation of Energy, what happens to the total amount of energy during a change?

quizzes.title: 🏛 How Energy Changes Form in Systems Quiz

questions.text: What is an energy transformation?

answers.text: Energy changing from one form to another
Energy staying in one form forever

questions.text: Which example shows an energy transformation?

answers.text: Electrical energy turning into heat in a toaster
A book resting on a table

questions.text: In a flashlight, what sequence of energy transformations occurs?
What is a system in the study of energy?

answers.text: The object or group of objects being studied

questions.text: Which observation is evidence that energy has transformed?

answers.text: Temperature increases or sound is produced

questions.text: Which type of radiation is felt as heat?

questions.text: What are the three main ways light can interact with materials?

Light traveling at different speeds in different materials

answers.text: They allow light to pass through

questions.text: What does a wave transfer?

answers.text: The material a wave travels through

questions.text: Which type of wave can travel through empty space?

answers.text: Because particles interact differently in each material
Because waves only move in one direction
Because all materials are the same

questions.text: Which type of wave can travel through empty space?

What type of energy is stored in food and batteries?

answers.text: Particles in solids are closer together

questions.text: Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum can humans see?
Which process changes a liquid into a gas?

What occurs when light bends as it passes from one material to another?
Heat naturally flows from:
Which material allows most light to pass through clearly?

What is thermal equilibrium?

answers.text: When two objects reach the same temperature

questions.text: Which example demonstrates mechanical energy?

answers.text: Energy cannot be created or destroyed

questions.text: Which wave requires a medium to travel?

answers.text: A solid changes to a liquid

questions.text: Which color of visible light has the shortest wavelength?

answers.text: Waves transfer energy from one place to another

questions.text: Which process occurs when a solid changes directly into a liquid?
Why is radiation important for life on Earth?

answers.text: It allows sound to travel through space

questions.text: Where does Earth’s internal heat come from?

answers.text: Heat from earthquakes and volcanoes at the surface
Heat from ocean basins as they grow wider
Heat left over from Earth’s formation and heat from radioactive elements
Heat from mountains pushing together as they form

questions.text: What is convection?

answers.text: The movement of material caused by heat differences
The uplift of Earth’s crust over time
Ground shaking caused by sudden energy release

questions.text: Mantle material near the core heats up. What happens to it next?

answers.text: It becomes more dense and sinks
It becomes less dense and rises slowly
It turns into lava inside the core
It stays in place because rock cannot move

questions.text: Which surface change happens slowly, over millions of years?

answers.text: The location where two plates meet
A large piece of Earth’s crust that moves over the mantle
The layer beneath the crust where material can flow slowly
Movement caused by heat differences inside Earth

questions.text: What powers the movement of tectonic plates?

answers.text: Continental crust sliding on oceanic crust
Heat inside Earth and convection in the mantle

questions.text: What happens at a divergent boundary?

answers.text: Plates move away from each other, and magma rises to make new crust
Plates move toward each other, and one plate may sink
Plates slide past each other, and stress builds up
Plates collide and crumple into mountains

answers.text: New crust forming at an ocean ridge

questions.text: True or false: Every tectonic plate is made of only continental crust.
How do igneous rocks form?

answers.text: Sediment is compacted and cemented in layers
Existing rock is changed by heat and pressure without melting
Wind and water break rock into small pieces

answers.text: Deposition, erosion, weathering, compaction and cementation
Erosion, compaction and cementation, weathering, deposition
Weathering, erosion, deposition, compaction and cementation
Compaction and cementation, deposition, erosion, weathering

answers.text: The exact age of an object in years
Whether something is older or younger than something else
How much of a radioactive element remains
The time it takes for half of an element to decay

questions.text: A road cut shows five flat, undisturbed rock layers. From the top down they are labeled A, B, C, D, and E. Which layer formed first?

answers.text: Layer B, just below the top

questions.text: What is a half-life?

answers.text: The time it takes for half of a radioactive element to decay
The vast span of time covering Earth’s history
The age of something compared to other objects
The order of rock layers from bottom to top

answers.text: Comparing which layer is on top
Finding which layer holds a fossil

The movement of soil or rock by natural forces

The parking lot works like a dam and holds water back
Urban heat islands melt ice into the rivers
